evidence.reference_title: BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations from 97 patients.
evidence.snippet: Most of them had cerebellar ataxia (82%), axial hypotonia (79%) and cerebellar atrophy (100%).

evidence.reference_title: BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations from 97 patients.
evidence.snippet: BRAT1 biallelic variants are associated with rigidity and multifocal seizure syndrome, lethal neonatal (RMFSL), and neurodevelopmental disorder associating cerebellar atrophy with or without seizures syndrome (NEDCAS).

nodes.description: Biallelic BRAT1 variants (usually with at least one hypomorphic missense allele in NEDCAS) reduce BRAT1 protein and its binding to the Integrator cleavage module.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous pathogenic variant in BRAT1 associated with nonprogressive cerebellar ataxia.
evidence.snippet: Western blotting revealed markedly decreased BRAT1 protein levels in lymphocytes and/or fibroblast cells from both affected siblings compared to control cell lines.

evidence.reference_title: BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations from 97 patients.
evidence.snippet: genotypes with at least one missense were more likely associated with NEDCAS

nodes.description: Cerebellar atrophy on MRI, usually stable/nonprogressive; the defining imaging feature.

evidence.reference_title: BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations from 97 patients.
evidence.snippet: Most of them had cerebellar ataxia (82%), axial hypotonia (79%) and cerebellar atrophy (100%).

nodes.description: Reduced Integrator cleavage activity impairs 3'-end processing of small nuclear RNAs (notably U1), snoRNAs and histone pre-mRNAs; unprocessed U1 snRNA accumulates, and the degree of misprocessing scales with clinical severity.

evidence.reference_title: Unprocessed U1 snRNAs as a biomarker of INTS11- and BRAT1-related neurodevelopmental disorders.
evidence.snippet: The magnitude of U1 snRNA misprocessing closely correlates with clinical severity across the BRAT1 cohort, highlighting its potential as a diagnostic biomarker.

nodes.description: BRAT1 is a cytoplasmic chaperone that binds and stabilizes the INTS9/INTS11 cleavage heterodimer of the Integrator complex; loss of BRAT1 lowers INTS11 stability and impairs Integrator assembly/function.

evidence.reference_title: BRAT1 links Integrator and defective RNA processing with neurodegeneration.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that BRAT1 tightly interacts with INTS9/INTS11 subunits of the Integrator complex that processes 3' ends of various noncoding RNAs and pre-mRNAs.

evidence.reference_title: Cytoplasmic binding partners of the Integrator endonuclease INTS11 and its paralog CPSF73 are required for their nuclear function.
evidence.snippet: stabilizes INTS11 in the cytoplasm and is required for Integrator function in the nucleus

evidence.reference_title: BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations from 97 patients.

nodes.description: The RNA-processing disturbance is inferred to derail neurodevelopmental gene expression in the cerebellum, producing cerebellar atrophy, ataxia, intellectual disability and, in some patients, seizures. The step is shown at the molecular level and in model systems; its operation in human cerebellar neurons is inferred.

evidence.reference_title: BRAT1 links Integrator and defective RNA processing with neurodegeneration.
evidence.snippet: Collectively, our data suggest that defects in BRAT1 interfere with proper Integrator functions, leading to incorrect expression of RNAs and proteins, resulting in neurodegeneration.

evidence.reference_title: BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations from 97 patients.
evidence.snippet: Most of them had cerebellar ataxia (82%), axial hypotonia (79%) and cerebellar atrophy (100%).

nodes.description: Intellectual disability, ranging from mild (NPCA) to severe; a defining feature.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous pathogenic variant in BRAT1 associated with nonprogressive cerebellar ataxia.
evidence.snippet: We report 2 brothers with a novel homozygous BRAT1 variant who present with a much milder phenotype than reported in the literature to date, with mild intellectual disability, nonprogressive cerebellar ataxia (NPCA), and stable cerebellar atrophy on serial brain imaging.

evidence.reference_title: BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations from 97 patients.
evidence.snippet: Nystagmus was reported in 23 patients (23/28; 82%), oculomotor apraxia in 6 (6/17; 35%) and strabismus in 8 (8/16; 50%).

nodes.description: Epilepsy occurs in a minority (about 16%), with a median onset around 3 years; hence "with or without seizures".

evidence.reference_title: BRAT1-related disorders: phenotypic spectrum and phenotype-genotype correlations from 97 patients.
evidence.snippet: Epilepsy occured in 6 individuals (6/38; 16%). The mean age of onset was 4 years and 5 months (median: 3 years 1 month) ranging from 3 months to 13 years.

nodes.description: Homozygous c.185T>A (p.Val62Glu); causes the mild nonprogressive cerebellar ataxia (NPCA) presentation with markedly reduced BRAT1 protein.
